header.running_head: Relationships between Men, Women and Children

blocks.text: Hafsah (RA) told her. The tent was made of palm leaves and was a hiding place for the people. It was however filled with dirt and spider webs. Hadhrat Sauda (RA) went to hide there as Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived. Seeing the two women laughing so much that they were unable to talk, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What is all the laughter about?" Rasulullaah ﷺ had to repeat the question thrice before they pointed towards the tent. Rasulullaah ﷺ went to the tent where he found Hadhrat Sauda (RA) shivering (with fear). "What is the matter, O Sauda?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" she said, "The one-eyed one has appeared." "He has not appeared," Rasulullaah ﷺ clarified, "but he is still to appear. He has not appeared but is still to appear." Rasulullaah ﷺ then helped her out and dusted the dirt and spider webs off her. [^1]
Another narration adds that Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) said to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), "Rasulullaah ﷺ is coming to see us and we are looking so unkempt while she is gleaming between us." [^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Relationship with Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting down when he heard the people and children making a lot of noise. (When he looked out) He saw some Abyssinians dancing with the people around them. 'O Aa'isha!' Rasulullaah ﷺ called out, 'Come and have a look.' Placing my cheek against his shoulder, I started looking from between his shoulders and head. 'O Aa'isha,' Rasulullaah ﷺ kept saying (as I kept looking for a long time), 'have you not had your fill?' To assess my status with Rasulullaah ﷺ, I kept saying that I had not. I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ taking support on one leg and then the other (as he grew tired of standing so long). When Umar (RA) appeared, the people and children all dispersed and Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, 'I see the human and Jinn devils all flee from Umar (RA).'" The narration still continues further. [^3]

In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "By Allaah! I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ standing at the door of my room as some Abyssinians amused the people with their spears in the (courtyard of the) Masjid. Rasulullaah ﷺ screened me with his shawl as I watched their feats from between his ear and shoulder. Rasulullaah ﷺ then remained standing because of me until I (grew tired and) turned away. You can well imagine how eager a young girl (as I) is for amusement (and for how long I stood watching)." [^4]
